title: One show, one snack, three towns: Wagga Wagga’s Chiko Roll moment
dek: A one-minute history of the Chiko Roll’s documented 1951 Wagga Wagga debut—and why that does not settle where it was invented.
author: Al Zadid Yusuf

paragraphs: Wagga Wagga did not simply “invent” the Chiko Roll. Its more defensible claim is just as interesting: the city hosted the snack’s documented public breakthrough.

list.label: Developed in Victoria.
list.text: Bendigo boilermaker and caterer Frank McEncroe developed a sturdier, one-handed alternative to a chop-suey roll he had seen outside a Richmond football ground.

list.label: Launched in Wagga.
list.text: The new roll appeared at the 1951 Wagga Wagga Agricultural Show. The Australian Dictionary of Biography says it was acclaimed there; Wagga Wagga City Council describes the event as its first commercial sale.

list.label: Claimed by several places.
list.text: Wagga, Bendigo and Bathurst later argued over the snack’s home. The council itself calls Wagga’s “birthplace” claim controversial and records the manufacturer’s position that the origins are varied and complex.

sections.heading: What Wagga can confidently claim
paragraphs: Wagga was the launch stage, not the whole origin story. For the Chiko Roll’s fiftieth anniversary, its manufacturer presented gold-plated rolls to both Wagga and Bendigo—a fittingly shared memorial to a famously disputed snack.
